source: Ported from the govbot witness-slip draft (state participation directory).

jurisdictions.name: Alabama
jurisdictions.how_to: Alabama has no statewide witness-slip or e-comment portal. You testify in person or email the committee chair listed on the hearing notice.

jurisdictions.name: Alaska
jurisdictions.how_to: Alaska does not use Illinois-style slips. Residents send a Public Opinion Message (POM) or sign up to testify when a committee is hearing a bill.

jurisdictions.name: Arizona
jurisdictions.how_to: Arizona’s Request to Speak (RTS) system is the closest cousin of an Illinois witness slip: you register a position and may request time at the hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Arkansas
jurisdictions.how_to: Arkansas does not run a public slip portal. Appear in committee or write the chair using the hearing notice.

jurisdictions.name: California
jurisdictions.how_to: California has no witness slips. The Assembly Position Letter Portal and committee email are how you register support, opposition, or written testimony.

jurisdictions.name: Colorado
jurisdictions.how_to: Colorado lets you sign in for in-person, remote, or written testimony when a committee posts a hearing — not a standing slip on every bill.

jurisdictions.name: Connecticut
jurisdictions.how_to: Connecticut committees post how to email or upload written testimony on each hearing agenda. There is no statewide slip ledger.

jurisdictions.name: Delaware
jurisdictions.how_to: Delaware House committees often take virtual public comment through the meeting calendar. Senate practice is committee-by-committee.

jurisdictions.name: District of Columbia
jurisdictions.how_to: The DC Council posts witness sign-up and written testimony instructions on each hearing notice. That is their version of a slip.

jurisdictions.name: Florida
jurisdictions.how_to: Florida uses Appearance Request forms (House and Senate) to speak in committee. That is not a remote position slip — you are asking to appear.

jurisdictions.name: Georgia
jurisdictions.how_to: Georgia has no statewide e-slip system. Public input is in-person testimony or email to the committee listed on the agenda.

jurisdictions.name: Guam
jurisdictions.how_to: Guam’s Legislature posts bills and hearing notices. Public comment is the island’s analogue to a witness slip.

jurisdictions.name: Hawaii
jurisdictions.how_to: Hawaii’s Capitol site lets you submit written or remote testimony on a measure once you have an account — one of the more complete portals outside Illinois.

jurisdictions.name: Idaho
jurisdictions.how_to: Idaho puts remote-testify links on each committee agenda. There is no standing slip on a bill before a hearing is posted.

jurisdictions.name: Illinois
jurisdictions.how_to: Illinois is the national model: my.ilga.gov lets you record support, opposition, or no position on a bill when a committee hearing is posted.

jurisdictions.name: Indiana
jurisdictions.how_to: Indiana uses an Appearance Form to speak in committee. It is a request to testify, not a tally of positions like an Illinois slip.

jurisdictions.name: Iowa
jurisdictions.how_to: Iowa takes written comments and Zoom remarks on subcommittee and public-hearing pages. Comment opens when that meeting is posted.

jurisdictions.name: Kansas
jurisdictions.how_to: Kansas has no statewide slip portal. Written testimony is emailed to the committee assistant named on the agenda.

jurisdictions.name: Kentucky
jurisdictions.how_to: Kentucky committees post a Testimony Request form. You are asking to speak; there is no public pro/con slip count.

jurisdictions.name: Louisiana
jurisdictions.how_to: Louisiana still uses in-room witness cards at committee. There is no statewide e-slip desk.

jurisdictions.name: Maine
jurisdictions.how_to: Maine’s testimony form covers Zoom testimony and written remarks for a public hearing — the state’s stand-in for a slip.

jurisdictions.name: Maryland
jurisdictions.how_to: Maryland’s MyMGA portal is the other big sibling of Illinois slips: online witness signup and testimony upload for House and Senate hearings.

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts
jurisdictions.how_to: Massachusetts has no single slip site. Written testimony is emailed to the committee hosting the hearing; some hearings also take Zoom remarks.

jurisdictions.name: Michigan
jurisdictions.how_to: Michigan does not publish a statewide e-comment ledger. You testify in person or send remarks to the clerk on the committee notice.

jurisdictions.name: Minnesota
jurisdictions.how_to: Minnesota House and Senate each post how to testify and how to send written comments when a hearing is scheduled.

jurisdictions.name: Mississippi
jurisdictions.how_to: Mississippi has no public e-slip system. Appear in committee or write the chair.

jurisdictions.name: Missouri
jurisdictions.how_to: Missouri House has an online Witness Form; the Senate has a Witness Registration System. Both record your position for a hearing.

jurisdictions.name: Montana
jurisdictions.how_to: Montana’s Public Participation app covers remote testimony, written comment, and short messages to a committee — their version of a slip.

jurisdictions.name: Nebraska
jurisdictions.how_to: Nebraska’s unicameral posts hearing comments online. You register a position when a public hearing is set, not on every introduced bill.

jurisdictions.name: Nevada
jurisdictions.how_to: Nevada’s NELIS system is how the public submits comments and exhibits on bills during session.

jurisdictions.name: New Hampshire
jurisdictions.how_to: New Hampshire committees take sign-up for remote or in-person testimony from the General Court calendar. No statewide slip count.

jurisdictions.name: New Jersey
jurisdictions.how_to: New Jersey posts committee agendas with instructions to submit written testimony. There is no Illinois-style public slip tally.

jurisdictions.name: New Mexico
jurisdictions.how_to: New Mexico uses online witness signup around committee hearings. Comment is tied to the hearing, not a standing bill ledger.

jurisdictions.name: New York
jurisdictions.how_to: New York Senate and Assembly each collect written and in-person hearing testimony. There is no unified witness-slip dashboard.

jurisdictions.name: North Carolina
jurisdictions.how_to: North Carolina publishes committee calendars; some committees take online public comment. Practice varies by chair.

jurisdictions.name: North Dakota
jurisdictions.how_to: North Dakota’s legislature site hosts hearing documents and testimony during the biennial session.

jurisdictions.name: Northern Mariana Islands
jurisdictions.how_to: The CNMI Legislature does not publish a statewide e-slip. Govbot still tracks its bills in the national index.

jurisdictions.name: Ohio
jurisdictions.how_to: Ohio still uses witness slips — usually attached to the committee notice. House has a standard form; Senate slips vary by committee.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma
jurisdictions.how_to: Oklahoma does not offer a statewide e-slip. Testimony is in committee or by writing the chair.

jurisdictions.name: Oregon
jurisdictions.how_to: Oregon opens online witness registration when a public hearing is scheduled and usually closes it 30 minutes before the gavel.

jurisdictions.name: Pennsylvania
jurisdictions.how_to: Pennsylvania committees take written testimony by email. There is no public statewide slip ledger.

jurisdictions.name: Puerto Rico
jurisdictions.how_to: Puerto Rico’s Assembly takes written testimony (ponencias) on measures. Govbot tracks those bills in the same national index.

jurisdictions.name: Rhode Island
jurisdictions.how_to: Rhode Island posts hearing notices with instructions to submit written testimony to the committee.

jurisdictions.name: South Carolina
jurisdictions.how_to: South Carolina has no e-slip portal. Appear in committee or write the chair listed on the agenda.

jurisdictions.name: South Dakota
jurisdictions.how_to: South Dakota’s legislature site hosts bills and hearing documents during session. Written comments go to the committee.

jurisdictions.name: Tennessee
jurisdictions.how_to: Tennessee does not run a public slip desk. Testimony is in committee or by contacting members.

jurisdictions.name: Texas
jurisdictions.how_to: Texas House witness registration is how the public records a position or asks to testify. The Senate uses committee clerk processes.

jurisdictions.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
jurisdictions.how_to: The Virgin Islands Legislature takes committee testimony on bills. Govbot indexes those measures in the national dashboard.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.how_to: Congress does not use witness slips. House and Senate committees take written testimony for noticed hearings, and you can write your members on any bill.

jurisdictions.name: Utah
jurisdictions.how_to: Utah’s legislature site takes public comments on bills during session. That comment is their analogue to a slip.

jurisdictions.name: Vermont
jurisdictions.how_to: Vermont committees accept written testimony by email and sometimes remote remarks. No statewide slip count.

jurisdictions.name: Virginia
jurisdictions.how_to: Virginia’s LIS pages and committee sites collect comments around hearings. There is no unified slip ledger like Illinois.

jurisdictions.name: Washington
jurisdictions.how_to: Washington’s Committee Sign-In is the state’s witness slip: register to testify or submit written comments, usually until 24 hours after the hearing starts.

jurisdictions.name: West Virginia
jurisdictions.how_to: West Virginia has no statewide e-slip. Public input is in-person or written to the committee.

jurisdictions.name: Wisconsin
jurisdictions.how_to: Wisconsin uses hearing registration and written testimony through the legislature’s site when a public hearing is noticed.

jurisdictions.name: Wyoming
jurisdictions.how_to: Wyoming is a small, in-person legislature. There is no e-slip desk; you appear or write the committee.
